title: Introduction to Verbal Aspect
intro: Russian verbs come in pairs! Almost every verb has two forms: IMPERFECTIVE (несовершенный вид) for ongoing, repeated, or incomplete actions, and PERFECTIVE (совершенный вид) for completed, single, or result-focused actions. This is called 'aspect' - вид глагола. Understanding aspect is essential because Russians choose between these forms constantly. Think of imperfective as 'process' and perfective as 'result'.
rules: Russian verbs have two aspects: imperfective (НСВ) and perfective (СВ): читать (НСВ) / прочитать (СВ).
Imperfective = process, duration, repetition, ongoing action: Я читал книгу (I was reading).
Perfective = completion, result, single completed action: Я прочитал книгу (I finished reading).
Aspect pairs are formed by prefixes (делать → сделать), suffixes (решать → решить), or different stems (брать → взять).
examples: Я читал книгу весь день. (I was reading a book all day., imperfective), process
Я прочитал книгу. (I finished the book., perfective), completed result
Она писала письмо. (She was writing a letter., imperfective), in progress
Она написала письмо. (She wrote/finished the letter., perfective), done

items.prompt: Я долго _____ книгу. (I read a book for a long time.)
items.promptEnglish: I read a book for a long time.
items.explanation: Duration words like 'долго' require imperfective aspect.

items.prompt: Вчера я _____ эту книгу. (Yesterday I finished this book.)
items.explanation: Finishing something completely requires perfective aspect.

items.prompt: Which aspect focuses on the RESULT of an action?
items.promptEnglish: Which aspect focuses on the RESULT of an action?
items.explanation: Perfective aspect emphasizes completion and result.

items.prompt: Она каждый день _____ газету. (She reads the newspaper every day.)
items.promptEnglish: She reads the newspaper every day.

items.prompt: Я наконец _____ задачу! (I finally solved the problem!)
items.explanation: Success, completion, result all call for perfective.
Писать is imperfective; написать is its perfective pair.

items.prompt: Мы _____ обед два часа. (We were cooking dinner for two hours.)
items.promptEnglish: We were cooking dinner for two hours.
items.explanation: Duration of the action requires imperfective.

items.prompt: Он быстро _____ работу. (He quickly finished the work.)
items.explanation: Finishing something is a completed result: perfective.

blanks: Я весь вечер _____ телевизор. (I watched TV all evening.)
hints: The phrase 'весь вечер' (all evening) signals a duration. Which aspect describes ongoing actions?
explanations: Duration markers like весь вечер (all evening) require imperfective aspect: смотрел (was watching), not посмотрел (watched to completion).

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ книгу три часа. (I read for three hours.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I read the book for three hours.

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ книгу и вернул её в библиотеку. (I read the book and returned it.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I read the book and returned it to the library.
minimalPairs.explanation: Completed action (then returned) requires perfective: прочитал.

reviewVocab.definition: aspect pair (two forms of one verb)
